title: Making tricky plurals: words ending in y, f, and hissing sounds

blocks.content: Most words become plural by just adding -s: one book, two books. But some words are tricky. Let's learn three little tricks that catch a lot of people out.
Trick 1 — When a word ends in a consonant then y, change the y to i and add es.

steps: 'baby' ends in a consonant (b) then y.

blocks.explain: 'city' ends in a consonant (t) then y, so change y to i and add es: cities.
blocks.rule: If a word ends in a consonant then y, change the y to i and add es.

blocks.content: Trick 2 — When a word ends in f or fe, change the f to v and add es.

blocks.question: What is the plural of 'leaf'?
blocks.explain: 'leaf' ends in f, so change the f to v and add es: leaves.
blocks.rule: If a word ends in f or fe, change the f to v and add es.

blocks.content: Trick 3 — When a word ends in a hissing sound (s, x, ch, or sh), add es.

blocks.explain: 'bus' ends in the hissing sound s, so add es: buses.
blocks.rule: If a word ends in s, x, ch or sh, add es to make it plural.

blocks.content: Nice work! Three tricks: consonant + y turns to ies, f turns to ves, and hissing sounds add es. When a plural looks tricky, ask which trick fits. Time to practise!
